title: Sandbox run predicate v0.1
description: Predicate body of an in-toto Statement v1 with predicateType https://historlabs.eu/run/v0.1. Signed by the harness signing key. Everything needed to decide whether a run's stated outcome follows from what was actually run, WITHOUT access to the data. The verifier recomputes threshold outcomes from these numbers; if it cannot, the field is missing and the predicate is wrong.

run_number.description: Monotonic per sandbox, starting at 1. Contiguity is what stops a provider running ten times and reporting the best; the verifier checks for gaps.

backend.description: Where the run executed. Must agree with isolation_evidence.type: each backend can produce exactly one kind of isolation evidence, so a mismatch means the predicate claims more (or other) than happened.

harness_statement_digest.description: Digest of the harness's own signed statement of what it measured (harness-statements.jsonl in the bundle). The control plane completes this attestation; the harness signed its measurements in segment A, and the verifier checks the two agree. For a run scored off an HPC centre (driver_statement_digest present), the measurement statement is the scorer's, signed with the scorer key where the labels are.

driver_statement_digest.description: Only for a run whose scoring was kept off an HPC centre (spec/run-attestation.md, section 1b). Digest of the driver's signed statement of what it observed in the job (predicate type https://historlabs.eu/driver-observation/v0.1, signed with the harness key released to the job, carried in harness-statements.jsonl). The scorer's statement cites the same digest and the same responses; the verifier checks that the two agree and that each result's counts are the ones the driver observed.

initiated_by.description: Present only on a run the notified body initiated (AI Act Annex VII, point 4.4), as the gate's run_started entry says it. An ordinary run, requested by the regulator or the provider for a test in the plan, carries neither this nor authorisation.

authorisation.description: What authorised a run the notified body initiated, copied from its run_started entry: the proposal (its ledger seq and digest) and either the approvals the plan's notified_body_tests.approvers gave (route pre_authorised, the approvals' ledger seqs) or the amendment that adopted it (route amendment, the plan version and its plan_signed seq). The verifier walks this chain in the ledger (check nb_tests).

hardware.description: Results are valid for the hardware they were produced on and no other. GPU heterogeneity across EuroHPC centres makes this load-bearing rather than decorative.

node_id_hash.description: Hashed, not plain: the node identity must be comparable across runs without being disclosed.

seeds.description: Every seed used, in order. The harness always sends one; recording them is what makes determinism a test rather than a hope.

harness_config.description: How the request stream was built. In the attestation because 'the model could not infer the dataset boundaries' is a claim, and this is its evidence.

isolation_evidence.description: Tagged union. The verifier must handle both arms even though the MVP produces only cilium.

network_policy_digest.description: Must equal the plan's pin. Results produced under a different policy are results from a different experiment.

drop_log_digest.description: Digest over the Hubble drop events captured for this run. Blocked attempts are evidence, so an empty drop log is a claim in its own right.

image_signatures.description: Whether the sandbox itself verified the images' signatures before launch (histor/backends/imagesig.py), and against which policy. Optional: evidence made before it existed has none, and says nothing about signatures. verified: every image verified under the policy; partially_verified: the policy had rules for some images only, and those verified; not_verified_by_sandbox: no policy was configured, so the sandbox checked nothing and signature_verified in the ledger is only the host's statement. A failed check never appears here, because a run whose images fail is not launched.

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the policy's rules, public keys included by content.

verifier.description: What checked the signatures, e.g. cosign.

images.description: Per workload: the reference checked (repository@digest) and its status.

isolation_hpc_centre.description: Where no user-controlled network policy exists, someone vouches for exclusive allocation and node configuration by signing the job record and the node configuration. signed_by says who: the centre, with its own key, or the sandbox operator, whose courier observed the job through the project's login. The operator's word is weaker than a centre's, and both are weaker than a policy anyone can hash; the verifier must name who signed rather than treating the arms as equivalent. An arm without signed_by predates it: it is the centre's, and its signature is in centre_signature.

signed_by.description: Whose word the claim rests on. centre: the centre's key, recorded in the ledger as hpc_centre_key. sandbox_operator: the sandbox operator's key, recorded as hpc_operator_key.

signature.description: Base64 of a DSSE envelope (histor/crypto/signing.py) over this object without its signature fields, signed with the key signed_by names.

centre_signature.description: The centre's signature, as signature, under its name before signed_by existed. Accepted only for the centre: without signed_by, or with signed_by centre.

measurement.description: A number and what makes it admissible. A bare scalar is not reportable: the exit report has to state how it was obtained and how uncertain it is, and the verifier cannot check a pass on a group of four items unless n is here.

method.description: How the value and interval were obtained: 'wilson', 'bootstrap(2000)', 'mean of 5 runs'.

insufficient_sample.description: True when n fell below the plan's min_items_per_group. The value is then reported for completeness and MUST NOT be scored against a threshold.

metrics.description: Overall measurement per metric name, e.g. {"mae": {...}}.

by_group.description: metric name -> group attribute -> group value -> measurement. For adversarial_robustness the attribute 'attack' holds one rate per planned attack; for fail_safe the attribute 'input_kind' holds one rate per kind of out-of-scope input. Those are conditions, not demographic groups, and never leave segment A as anything but these rates.

baseline.description: Same shape as metrics, for the plan's baseline predictor. Present whenever the plan declared a baseline other than none.

perturbation_curve.description: Robustness only: perturbation name -> parameter value -> measurement, so the degradation curve is in the evidence rather than a single before-and-after pair.

method_digest.description: adversarial_robustness and fail_safe: digest over the code that generated the inputs (the attacks or the out-of-scope generators). The plan fixes the parameters; this fixes what they mean.

thresholds_evaluated.description: Every threshold the plan set for this test, the observed value, and whether it held. The verifier recomputes these; a mismatch fails the bundle.

scope.description: Which group or perturbation the worst observed value came from, when the threshold is per-group.

isolation_local_process.description: No isolation was enforced. Emitted when a run happens on a developer machine or in CI, where the harness, the relay and the model are ordinary processes on one host with full network access. It exists so that such a run can still produce a well-formed attestation for development and demonstration — and so that it CANNOT be mistaken for one that was isolated. The alternative, emitting cilium-shaped evidence without Cilium, would be fabricating evidence. A verifier must report a bundle carrying this arm as unattested for isolation and must never pass it as sandbox evidence.

note.description: Why no isolation was enforced, in words a reader will see in the verifier's output.

model_egress.description: Where the model sent each item, when the provider forwards to a hosted model rather than running the weights itself. Present means the test data left the host: a verifier must say so beside the isolation caveat.

tee.description: Optional. Present when the run's keys were released to a trusted execution environment (TEE) on the strength of a hardware attestation report: what identifies that report and what it attests. The report itself, its collateral and the binding are in the run's key_released ledger entry, where the verifier checks them again (check tee_attestation). Platform mock is software made for tests and the demo and is never hardware evidence.

report_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw report bytes.

measurement.description: The launch measurement (SEV-SNP MEASUREMENT, TDX MRTD), lowercase hex.

init_data_digest.description: The launch configuration that pins the harness image (SEV-SNP HOST_DATA, TDX MRCONFIGID), lowercase hex.

tcb.description: The platform's TCB level by component: integers, or lowercase hex for TDX's tee_tcb_svn.

gpu.description: GPU attestation evidence, carried and not yet verified (phase P2).

collateral_digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the collateral captured at release time.
